I retested it with the latest Godot 4.6.1 release and the same Problem appears which makes Godot unusable for this (my) case.

This Time I did try to narrow the problem down even further by modifying the code and see how godot reacts.

Original Idea was to have some tick that lasts longer than the plugin object (in case it is deactivated). That is why I use this code:

```csharp
 EditorInterface.Singleton.GetEditorMainScreen().GetTree().ProcessFrame += GlobalProcessor;
```

It seems to try to call the GlobalProcessor method while the assembly is already unloaded. So I suspect that there is some reference not properly cleaned up. This leads me to the conclusion that GlobalProcessor is called, but the code of the godot backing object is already disposed (!). So all C#-World code still runs fine, but all objects on the godot side are disposed.

With my latest changes I could reduce the endless looping error to a single error (by exiting GlobalProcessor early with a bool check):

```
 ERROR: /root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/NativeInterop/ExceptionUtils.cs:113 - System.ArgumentException: An item with the same key has already been added. Key: Enaweg.Plugin.EEditorPluginBase
  ERROR:    at System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary`2.TryInsert(TKey key, TValue value, InsertionBehavior behavior)
  ERROR:    at System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary`2.Add(TKey key, TValue value)
  ERROR:    at Godot.Bridge.ScriptManagerBridge.ScriptTypeBiMap.Add(IntPtr scriptPtr, Type scriptType) in /root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.types.cs:line 30
  ERROR:    at Godot.Bridge.ScriptManagerBridge.TryReloadRegisteredScriptWithClass(IntPtr scriptPtr) in /root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.cs:line 681
```

This is one step close to being usable, but I suspect that the actual method is still called endlessly every frame wasting some CPU. An other problem is that a second AssemblyReload is not possible anymore as it outputs the `Failed to unload assemblies.` error.

Furthermore, I did switch from the `EditorInterface.Singleton.GetEditorMainScreen().GetTree().ProcessFrame` to the plugins `_Process(double delta)` which did not change behavior at all.  With this, I am out of guesses on why it still has old objects around. It seems that AssemblyUnload does not work at all, event the first time.

Finally found the Problem, far from what was expected so far by me.

What seems to have changed between Godot 4.4.x and newer versions is that you can not derive a base class for EditorPlugins. This Code will fail:

```csharp
#if TOOLS
using Godot;

namespace Enaweg.Plugin;

public abstract partial class PluginBase : EditorPlugin
{
}

[Tool]
public partial class ExtendedEditorPlugin : PluginBase
{
}
#endif
```

This will cause an exception on second Build and an "Failed to unload assemblies" on third build.

I'm going to close this issue since it looks like a duplicate of a few different issues mixed together.

For issues about signal connections or Callables being lost after a reload, see:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70026
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86244

For issues about being unable to unload/reload assemblies, see:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/78513

For issues about a duplicate key being added to `ScriptTypeBiMap`, see:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/110608

Specifically for that last one, it seems the issue is when defining multiple classes in a single `.cs` file which is not allowed by Godot. Try making sure each C# class is defined on its own separate `.cs` file with a filename that matches the C# class name exactly, and see if you can still reproduce the issue.
